svg.title: Absolute encoder: it knows the angle at power-on
svg.desc: Animated. Top view of a steering module with the absolute encoder on its steering axle, and a dial of what the encoder reads. The power goes off and the wheel is turned by hand to a new angle; when the power comes back on, the dial's needle points at the wheel's real angle at once. This repeats, turning the wheel back. The sensor on the module itself reads the real angle at power-on, every time. It is what offsets are measured against, and the truth the motor encoder is checked against. Slower than the motor encoder, and a 10-bit one is coarser too. On MAXSwerve it is the through-bore encoder on the steering axle.
